projects.title: PM2.5 Forecasting System
projects.summary: Learning how air pollution changes across space and time, using historical observations and weather inputs.
projects.context: Contributed to VibeCoders' winning solution and developed a modular PyTorch forecasting repository.

details.heading: The problem
details.text: Forecast future PM2.5 concentrations on a spatial grid from historical pollutant observations and meteorological variables.

details.heading: The implementation
details.text: Developed the modular forecasting repository, implementing a PyTorch model with multiscale encoding, ConvLSTM recurrence, attention, and wind-based spatial warping. The model uses 10 historical steps to generate 16 forecast steps on a 140 × 124 grid.

details.heading: An important decision
details.text: Model spatial relationships and time together, and include wind information to represent the movement of pollution across the grid.

details.heading: Evidence & scope
details.text: The official event archive confirms Team VibeCoders' first place in the Pollution Forecasting track. The personal repository provides a modular model, configuration, and inference workflow; the team repository preserves the competition submission.

projects.title: Hospital Management System
projects.summary: Connecting hospital workflows through a relational database, with role-specific access and reporting.
projects.context: A database application covering patient records, appointments, billing, and staff workflows.

details.heading: The problem
details.text: Keep connected hospital records consistent while providing different workflows for staff roles, from appointments and patient records to billing and reports.

details.heading: What I built
details.text: A PostgreSQL database application with a Python interface, six staff dashboards, stored procedures, reporting views, and JSONB audit records.

details.heading: An important decision
details.text: Use database triggers to check appointment conflicts and record changes in JSONB audit logs. Expose patient history, daily appointments, outstanding bills, and low stock through reporting views.

details.heading: Evidence & scope
details.text: An academic database application with the schema, SQL workflows, and Python interface available in the repository. The reporting views cover patient history, daily appointments, outstanding bills, and low stock.

experience.description: Worked on information retrieval for internal policies, SOPs, and technical documentation in a chemical manufacturing setting.

project.title: Enterprise Knowledge Copilot
project.summary: Making internal documents easier to search, with answers that point back to the source page.

details.heading: The problem
details.text: Useful information was spread across policies, SOPs, and technical documents. The project explores how to retrieve relevant passages and return answers with traceable source pages.

details.heading: What I built
details.text: A Python ingestion and retrieval workflow using Docling OCR, semantic search in ChromaDB, BM25 keyword search, reciprocal rank fusion, and FastAPI endpoints.

details.heading: An important decision
details.text: Combine semantic and keyword results so both meaning and exact terminology can contribute to retrieval. Preserve page information to make the cited evidence inspectable.

details.heading: Evidence & scope
details.text: The repository includes a 20-case model-judged evaluation harness covering faithfulness, context recall, answer relevance, latency, and intended refusals. The implementation and committed evaluation report are available to review.

research.title: VL-JEPA Framework
research.summary: Implementing a VL-JEPA framework for surveillance anomaly detection and natural-language descriptions of detected anomalies.

details.heading: Research focus
details.text: Detect anomalies in surveillance video and generate natural-language captions that describe them.

details.heading: Current work
details.text: Implementing the VL-JEPA framework with the UCA dataset and comparing results with CLIP and SigLIP 2. The work is ongoing; comparative findings are not yet available.
